classification.difficultyReason: Combine hourly cost with journey time, minimise a reciprocal objective function, justify the minimum and convert cents to dollars.

content.prompt: A truck travels 1500 km at an hourly cost given by $s^2+9000$ cents where $s$ is the average speed of the truck.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Show that the cost for the trip is given by $C=1500\left(s+\frac{9000}{s}\right)$.

answer.worked:
For speed $s>0$ in km h$^{-1}$, the journey time is
$$\begin{align*}t&=\frac{d}{s}\\t&=\frac{1500}{s}.\end{align*}$$
The trip cost in cents is
$$\begin{align*}C&=(s^2+9000)t\\C&=(s^2+9000)\left(\frac{1500}{s}\right)\\C&=\frac{1500}{s}(s^2+9000)\\C&=1500\left(s+\frac{9000}{s}\right).\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find, to the nearest km h$^{-1}$, the speed that minimises the cost of the trip.

answer.worked:
For $s>0$,
$$\begin{align*}C(s)&=1500s+\frac{13\,500\,000}{s}\\C'(s)&=1500-\frac{13\,500\,000}{s^2}.\end{align*}$$
At a stationary point,
$$\begin{align*}0&=1500-\frac{13\,500\,000}{s^2}\\0&=1500s^2-13\,500\,000\\s^2&=9000\\s&=30\sqrt{10}\\s&\approx94.8683.\end{align*}$$
The negative root is excluded because $s>0$.
$$C''(s)=\frac{27\,000\,000}{s^3}>0\quad(s>0).$$
Thus the stationary point is the global minimum on the positive-speed domain. The required speed is $95\text{ km h}^{-1}$ to the nearest km h$^{-1}$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the cost of the trip to the nearest dollar.

answer.worked:
Use the unrounded minimising speed:
$$\begin{align*}C(30\sqrt{10})&=1500\left(30\sqrt{10}+\frac{9000}{30\sqrt{10}}\right)\\C(30\sqrt{10})&=90\,000\sqrt{10}\text{ cents}.\end{align*}$$
Converting to dollars,
$$\begin{align*}\text{Cost}&=\frac{90\,000\sqrt{10}}{100}\\\text{Cost}&=900\sqrt{10}\text{ dollars}\\\text{Cost}&\approx\$2846.05.\end{align*}$$
The cost is $\$2846$ to the nearest dollar.
